title: DARPAN aero-pdm
tagline: AI-enabled digital twin for aero piston engine health monitoring, fault prediction and mission-reliability (SIH26054)

repoTree.name: darpan (package: aero-pdm)
repoTree.description: A pnpm monorepo. One-way package dependency graph, zero hardcoded engine numbers — every constant traces to a data file.

children.name: shared/
children.description: Types, constants, and the physics plant model itself.

children.name: src/plant/isa.ts
children.description: International Standard Atmosphere: sea-level constants, lapse rate, altitude→temperature/pressure/density.

children.name: src/plant/rotax916-plant.ts
children.description: The forward model: given (rpm, throttle, altitude, OAT [, faults]), predicts every sensor channel for a healthy or faulted engine. Used by both the simulator (to generate ground truth) and the detector (to generate expected values).

children.name: src/plant/envelope.ts
children.description: Time-limited and condition-limited operating envelope checks (e.g. 5-minute takeoff power cap).

children.name: src/plant/lag.ts
children.description: First-order lag model — thermal and pressure channels move toward their target over time, not instantly.

children.name: src/plant/climb.ts
children.description: Estimates climb/descent rate from excess power, so altitude becomes a live output of flying rather than a dial an operator sets.

children.name: src/plant/engine-baseline.ts
children.description: The single place deciding which published number comes from which engine variant (performance baseline vs transferred instrument-suite data).

children.name: packages/simulator/
children.description: Mission generation, fault injection, the SOP procedure state machine, sensor realism (noise, quantisation, instrument drift).

children.name: packages/features/
children.description: Turns raw snapshots into residuals, persistence-confirmed deviations (N-of-M confirmation), and the sensor-vs-engine instrumentation split.

children.name: packages/decision/
children.description: The physics-only fault detector, RUL/degradation-rate estimation (Theil-Sen), and the digital-thread evidence-chain logger.

children.name: packages/knowledge/
children.description: Baseline curves and the sensor registry.

children.name: packages/ingestion/
children.description: Pull-based replay bus — a stand-in for a real telemetry link.

children.name: packages/engine-host/
children.description: A standalone process running ONE live engine instance, streamed over Server-Sent Events so every viewer watches the same engine. Nothing imports it as a library — the UI reaches it over HTTP.

children.name: packages/ui/
children.description: The React/Vite dashboard: gauges, the 3D digital twin, analysis pages, the degradation log, mission reports.

children.name: data/corpus/
children.description: Vendored OEM/research source files, checksummed so they can never be silently hand-edited.

children.name: data/authored/
children.description: DARPAN's own calibrated values — every leaf carries a provenance tag explaining where the number came from.

children.name: tools/
children.description: gen-corpus.ts is the only code allowed to read data/ directly and turn it into typed constants. export-dataset.ts builds the ML training set from simulated missions.

children.name: ml/
children.description: train.py trains the gradient-boosting model; ablate.py runs the feature-ablation study that checks the model isn't just re-reading the physics detector's own output.

dataFlow.name: SimulatorEngine / replay bus
dataFlow.description: Produces one tick's raw sensor snapshot — either a live simulated mission or a replayed recording.

dataFlow.name: EngineSnapshot
dataFlow.description: Every sensor channel's raw value for this tick.

dataFlow.name: FeatureEngine → FeatureSnapshot
dataFlow.description: Computes residuals (observed − physics-predicted), plus both a lagged and an instantaneous baseline.

dataFlow.name: DecisionEngine → DecisionOutput
dataFlow.description: System risk score, active alerts, and each alert's own evidence chain.

dataFlow.name: UI + downstream consumers
dataFlow.description: The live dashboard; the forecast/RUL module (mission-ready duration, P10/P50/P90 projection); a labelled training-data recorder feeding the ML pipeline.

pages.name: Home
pages.role: Dashboard: condition band, gauges, AI degradation score, SOP phase rail, trend sparklines.

pages.name: Simulator
pages.role: FADEC-style lab console — fly a mission by hand, inject a catalogue fault, step through SOP phases.

pages.name: 3D Engine
pages.role: The holographic 3D digital twin — live health-tinted parts, fly-in camera on selection.

pages.name: Analysis
pages.role: Residual plots, per-cylinder view, fuel-efficiency panel, advisory history.

pages.name: Degradation
pages.role: Per-component episode log with separate operator vs. machine disposition.

pages.name: Mission Report
pages.role: A single mission's health report — exportable and archivable.

pages.name: Baselines
pages.role: The engine's own reference numbers per SOP phase, with narrow editable anchor points.

pages.name: ML Transparency
pages.role: The real, recorded model comparison numbers, ablation study, and declared limits.

pages.name: Training
pages.role: A library of recorded/exported flight CSVs, with fault labeling.

pages.name: Help
pages.role: Generated operator's manual, rendered from the same source constants as the rest of the app.

pages.name: About
pages.role: Generated system dossier — provenance and honest-limits summary.

intakes.name: Sim
intakes.description: A live, in-browser simulated engine the operator directly commands. This is where a mission is authored.

intakes.name: Logger
intakes.description: Pure playback of a previously recorded file — a real recording, or a Sim export. Never commandable.

intakes.name: Live
intakes.description: Watches a real engine process running as its own service, over a real network link. Deliberately read-only always, even though nothing physical is attached yet — a monitoring dashboard that could start or stop a real engine over a link is not made safe just because nothing real happens to be plugged in.
